headline: Margins improve as one-time gain drives profit surge
summary_short: Freshpet grew Q1 FY2026 net sales 13.1% y/y to $297.6M on 14.6% volume growth, with gross margin up 110bp to 40.5%; net income swung to $48.5M from a $12.7M loss a year ago, primarily on a $62.0M pre-tax gain from selling a non-controlling equity stake.
summary_long: Net sales rose 13.1% y/y (+4.4% q/q) to $297.6M on 14.6% volume growth, partly offset by 1.5% unfavorable price/mix. Gross margin expanded 110bp y/y to 40.5% on lower input costs and better plant-expense leverage. Operating income turned positive at $4.3M (from an $11.5M loss) as last year's distributor-transition and legal charges did not recur, despite higher media spend. Net income of $48.5M (versus a $12.7M loss) was driven mainly by a $62.0M pre-tax gain on selling a non-controlling equity stake, partly offset by a $17.0M rise in income tax expense tied to that gain. Cash rose to $381.4M (+37.2% q/q) after $95.5M of sale proceeds. No sales or margin guidance was given; management reiterated approximately $150M of FY2026 capex.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by volume gains of 14.6% across Grocery, Mass, International, and Digital plus the Pet Specialty and Club channel, partly offset by 1.5% unfavorable price/mix.
Gross margin rose 110bp y/y to 40.5% primarily due to lower input costs and improved leverage on plant expenses.
SG&A as a percentage of sales fell y/y mainly because last year's non-recurring distributor-transition and legal charges did not recur, partially offset by increased media spend.

The swing to profit was driven mainly by a $62.0M pre-tax gain from selling a non-controlling equity stake, plus higher sales and lower non-recurring SG&A, partly offset by a $17.0M increase in income tax expense tied to that gain.

Freshpet cites continued Freshpet Fridge rollout (approximately 30,425 stores) and volume-led demand as the growth engine; the company reduced 2025 manufacturing-expansion capex and expects further operational efficiencies to improve near-term cash flow.
